GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_4: Completing Dungeons also provide a skip through certain parts of the campaign, as the entrance point is earlier in the campaign while the exit from the Dungeon will be further ahead in a different point in the campaign. Completing a Dungeon for the first time can also grant two passive skill points and one idol slot upgrade.
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_5: As previously mentioned, each Dungeon has a special mechanic, and in order to complete the Dungeon it is strongly recommended to interact with it. This is done by using the skill that is provided inside each Dungeon (used with D by default).
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_7: Lightless Arbor is a Dungeon where you traverse through darkness with a burning light source that loses its power when you take damage. Enemies in the darkness also deal substantially higher damage and take less damage. You may slay certain enemies to refresh power of your light source. Should you complete the Dungeon, at the end of it awaits The Vaults of Uncertain Fate that you may spend all your hard earned gold away for great rewards.
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_8: Soulfire Bastion is a Dungeon where you fight through undead hordes with two strong damage types, using a Soulfire Shield that switches protection between the two damage types. It is fueled by Souls that you obtain from slaying enemies. These same Souls are then also used to gamble with the Soulfire Gambler at the end of the Dungeon for powerful items.
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_9: Temporal Sanctum is a Dungeon where you must travel between two different Eras to get through it, and at the end of it you’ll have the option to use The Eternity Cache to create a Legendary item by combining an Exalted and Unique item with Legenary Potential.
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_11: Dungeon Key Charms are modifier items that can be used to modify your Dungeon experience. For example, you can add lots of <link="loot lizards">Loot Lizards</link> or open a shortcut portal directly to fight the boss.
GameGuide.Dungeons_Paragraph_12: Dungeon Keys can be used to purchase Dungeon Key Charms in Divine Era’s Maj’elka.
GameGuide.RegionSelection_Paragraph_0: You can change your preferred server region at the login screen, but also in-game in the Gameplay section of the Settings window.
GameGuide.RegionSelection_Paragraph_1: If you are the leader of a party, you can change what region all servers for your party will be in by going to the Party tab of the Social menu (hotkey H by default). You can use this to pick a region that is between you and your party members to avoid large differences in latency, for example.
GameGuide.RegionSelection_Paragraph_2: When you change your region setting in-game, the region of your current server won''t change. The next time you request a new server it will be in your new preferred region. Monolith and Arena gameplay happens on a single server, so you will need to go to another type of zone first for the change to apply.
GameGuide.ItemGifting_Paragraph_0: Equippable items found while playing together with other players in an area are able to be gifted to everyone who was present as the item was found with no time limit, and has no costs unlike <link="merchant''s guild">trading</link>. Gifting can be done from the interact-menu for other players.
GameGuide.ItemGifting_Paragraph_2: When you have received a gift, an icon in the bottom-right corner of the screen indicates it. Gifting Window can be opened by clicking that icon, or by from your Inventory (bound to I by default) and clicking the Gifting -button.
GameGuide.ItemGifting_Paragraph_4: Items can also be gifted with the use of <link="resonance">Resonance</link> in situations where a player was not present at the time of the item dropping.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_0: Resonances are special items that expand <link="item gifting">Item Gifting</link>, allowing you to gift specific items to players you play with frequently, even if the item didn’t drop while you were playing with them. Resonances are specific to an individual player. For example, a Golden Resonance that resonates with Moxjet200 (can be seen in the tooltip of the Resonance) allows you to gift an item to Moxjet200.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_1: There are two different types of Resonance that allow you to gift different varieties of items. Both types of Resonances are rare, but Golden Resonances are the more common of the two. They allow you to gift any normal, magic, rare, set, or unique item. Obsidian Resonance are much rarer, and allow you to gift exalted and <link="legendary items">Legendary items</link>.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_3: Slaying enemies that grant experience have a chance to grant progress towards a specific Resonance to drop, and once a certain amount of progress is gained, the Resonance will drop. This progress is cumulative between different play sessions and characters within a <link="game mode">Game Mode</link>, so when they share a stash, and only resets for a specific Resonance type when it is found.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_4: Gifting an item with Resonance that has any restriction does not remove or change that restriction. For example, an item that requires to be aligned with <link="circle of fortune">Circle of Fortune</link> to be equipped will still have that requirement after it was gifted.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_5: Resonances are stored when you press the “Transfer Materials” button in your inventory, and can be found in your Gifting window. You can open your gifting window by pressing “Gifting” button in your inventory.
GameGuide.Resonance_Paragraph_6:
Frequently Asked Questions:

Can I gain experience at max level (100)?

- Yes.

Can I gain experience at high level while playing in a low level area? For example, level 99 in a level 3 area.

- Yes. You won’t get much experience, but slaying any enemy that grants experience can generate progress, and the amount doesn’t matter.

Can I generate progress towards a Resonance just by being in a party with someone?
- No. You need to be in the same area and within a relatively close proximity. The distance is similar to experience gain range.

Can I track the progress towards a specific Resonance somehow?

- No, the progress towards Resonance drops is hidden.
GameGuide.GameMode_Paragraph_0: When creating a new character, on top of deciding whether a character will be a <link="season">Season</link> or <link="legacy">Legacy</link> character, there’s also other options: Game Mode and Challenges.
GameGuide.GameMode_Paragraph_1: There are two Game Modes in Last Epoch, Normal and Hardcore. The differences of the two are that they do not share stashes between eachother, and if a Hardcore character dies, it will become a Normal character of the same challenge and Season.
GameGuide.GameMode_Paragraph_2: There’s also additional <link="challenges">Challenges</link> that can be chosen to further customize your experience.
GameGuide.Challenges_Paragraph_0: When creating a character, on top choosing a <link="game mode">Game Mode</link>, additional challenges can be chosen: Solo Account Found (SAF) or Solo Character Found (SCF). This is not a permanent decision and you can opt-out from challenges in options.
GameGuide.Challenges_Paragraph_1: Solo Account Mode (SAF) characters are unable to party with nor obtain items found by other players. This also includes any items found with Solo Character Found characters even if they share the same game mode and Season. However, items found by other Solo Account Mode characters will share the stash and <link="item factions">Item Faction</link> progress in the same game mode and Season
GameGuide.Challenges_Paragraph_2: All characters created in Offline are by default Solo Account Found characters, unless opted-in for Solo Character Found. You can opt-out of Solo Account Found and turn the character to just Normal or Hardcore character with no extra challenges if it''s an Online character.
GameGuide.Challenges_Paragraph_3: Solo Character Found (SCF) is an added challenge to Solo where only items found by that character can be used by it, and no stash or Item Faction progress is shared with any other characters, even by your other Solo Character Found characters. You can opt-out of Solo Account Mode and turn the character to Solo Account Found to gain access to shared progress of other Solo Account Mode characters.
GameGuide.Legacy_Paragraph_0: Legacy is the permanently existing environment in Last Epoch, where all your previous characters and progress from <link="season">Season</link> will be transferred over to when those Season end. Legacy does not have competitive leaderboards that can be participated in. While a Season is active, some features from that Season may not be included or obtainable in Legacy. An example of that could be Season-restricted items. Currently, there are no Season-restricted items in Last Epoch.
GameGuide.Cycle_Paragraph_0: Seasons are periods of time with new content additions, changes to game balance and the reset of competitive leaderboards. It is also a fresh start where everyone making a character at the start of a new Season will start from scratch.
GameGuide.Cycle_Paragraph_1: While Season is active, you can choose to create a character in the current Season, or in Legacy. All Seasonal characters will transfer to <link="legacy">Legacy</link> at the end of a Season and all progress will carry over and will not be deleted.
GameGuide.Cycle_Paragraph_2: During a Season, some features may only be available in the Seasonal environment. An example of that could be Season-restricted items.
GameGuide.Cycle_Paragraph_3: If dying with a character that is playing Hardcore <link="game mode">Game Mode</link> in a Season, that character will not become a Normal Legacy character, but instead Normal Season character.
GameGuide.Arena_Paragraph_0: Arena is one of the endgame activies in Last Epoch, and is located in Champion’s Gate. If you have an Arena Key or Arena Key of Memory, you can right click it and it’ll open the world map and show the location of Champion’s Gate.
GameGuide.Arena_Paragraph_1: There’s two different modes in Arena: Arena Champions and Endless Arena.
GameGuide.Arena_Paragraph_2: Arena Champions consists of 40 waves with additional rewards that can be chosen, and eventually culminates in fighting an Arena Champion. There are 4 different tiers of Arena Champions with better rewards at higher tiers.
GameGuide.Arena_Paragraph_4: Endless Arena is a mode with unlimited waves that progressively become more and more difficult, and the best Arena runs will be visible in the Leaderboards (opened by pressing L by default). Leaderboards are only available in Online play in a <link="season">Season</link>. Climb the waves in Endless Arena to show how good you and your builds are!
GameGuide.Arena_Paragraph_5: Characters below level 50 will not be able to benefit from experience bonuses in Endless Arena.
GameGuide.LootFilter_Paragraph_0: Loot Filter is a tool that helps in filtering out items you might not want to pick up, or to enhance the display of items you do want to pick up. Having a Loot Filter feature in the game helps in allowing the loot drops to be plentiful and customizable to your specific needs. You can open the Loot Filter User Interface by clicking SHIFT + F by default.
GameGuide.LootFilter_Paragraph_1: A single Loot Filter can have up to 75 individual rules, and these rules can be freely moved around or disabled without needing to delete them.
GameGuide.LootFilter_Paragraph_3: The rules at the top of the the filter take priority over rules below them. For example, if the top rule in the filter would be “show Unique helmets”, and a rule below it that would be “hide all helmets”, you’d see all Unique helmets while rest of them would be hidden.
GameGuide.LootFilter_Paragraph_4: Loot Filters can be exported and imported directly in the User Interface without closing the game. Filters exist in a folder that can be opened from the UI, and placing another filter there will make it available to be used in-game, but a filter can also be imported directly from copying it if your clipboard has a valid Loot Filter saved on it.
GameGuide.LootFilter_Paragraph_5: When a Loot Filter is enabled, it is possible to temporarily disable it by holding a keybind (X by default).

GameGuide.ExiledMages_Paragraph_1: Exiled Mages are powerful mages imprisoned and banished through time by the leaders of an order of Runemasters for their crimes.
GameGuide.ExiledMages_Paragraph_3: Free them from their Rune Prisons if you dare, as untold eons of imprisonment may have driven them mad. The knowledge of the Exiled Mages can be found in the form of powerful items they experimented with, though this knowledge shall remain if you do not accept the risk and free them.
GameGuide.ExiledMages_Paragraph_4: Through <link="woven echoes">Woven Echoes</link>, you may be able to learn the secret to crafting your own <link="experimental items">Experimental Items</link>.
GameGuide.Nemesis_Paragraph_0: Nemeses are formed from the remaining equipment of powerful warriors slain by the <link="Harbingers">Harbingers</link>. Animated by the Harbingers'' lingering aura of despair, their animosity towards those that slew their former bearers extends to all travelers, not just those who serve Orobyss as Harbingers. They lie in wait for one to attempt to claim their items, and then coalesce into a formidable being of metal and wrath to exact vengeance.
GameGuide.Nemesis_Paragraph_2: Free them from their torment and use the trapped magic to empower items as your reward. Some Nemeses in the endgame may even allow you to exchange their unique for one of the player''s unique items with no <link="Legendary Items">Legendary Potential</link> or <link="Weaver''s Will">Weaver''s Will</link>, allowing it to be transformed into a Legendary or to be enhanced with Legendary Potential.
GameGuide.Nemesis_Paragraph_4:
When interacting with the Nemesis, there are 3 options to choose from:

<#E5E5E5>Banish</color> will remove the Nemesis and avoid a fight, but any items that replaced a Nemesis Egg will be lost. Your next Nemesis encounter will be with a new Nemesis that will have a fresh set of rewards.

<#E5E5E5>Challenge</color> will start the fight with the Nemesis and if defeated, will grant its items as rewards. Your next Nemesis encounter will be with a new Nemesis that will have a new set of item rewards.

<#E5E5E5>Empower</color> will start the fight with the Nemesis and if defeated, it will escape through a rift. You will then encounter this same Nemesis later, and it and its items have been Empowered. This upgrades items in various ways, such as gaining affixes, increasing tiers of existing affixes, or adding <link="forging potential">Forging Potential</link>. You can choose to Empower the Nemesis and its items twice before you must either Challenge or Banish it.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_1: The Map of Eterra (bound to M by default) provides lots of useful information about the world. You can find important story locations, keep track of your campaign progression, use waypoints to travel between different areas and Eras, and see how time and the Void has shaped the world from what it once was.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_3: At the top of the World Map UI, you can see a timeline with four different periods of time, or Eras. Through your travels in Eterra you visit these different Eras many times, and by clicking at any of them you can see the what Eterra looks like in different Eras throughout its history.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_5: On the left side of the World Map, you have a quest log that consists of your current active main and side quests, completed quests and the ability to pin or unpin quests that are then shown on the right side of your UI while you are playing.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_6: Clicking on a quest will bring a more detailed quest information and changes the Era of your UI and show where and when that quest is located at.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_7: Main quests are displayed with golden color, while side quests are in silver.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_9: You can also hover on a specific area or Era that has quest icons to see the names of those quests, and by right-clicking on an area with a unlocked waypoint you can immediately travel there from anywhere.
GameGuide.WorldMap_Paragraph_11: At the bottom left corner you can see how many of the maximum unlockable passive point and idol slot quest rewards you have obtained from completing quests. There are much more quests providing these rewards than the maximum, so you can choose to complete different quests while being able to get the maximum passive point and idol slot rewards.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_1: Experience is gained by completing quests, slaying enemies and from other rewards, such as <link="monolith introduction">Monolith</link> Echoes. As you gain experience, your character and skills will <link="levels">level up</link>, allowing you to customize and make your character stronger. The maximum character level in Last Epoch is 100. You can still gain experience at level 100, it just won’t increase character level anymore.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_3: A common way to increase the amount of experience gained is by increasing Corruption in Monolith of Fate, but there are other ways to increase experience such as Experience Shrines. Items in Last Epoch do not provide bonuses to experience gained.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_5: Magic enemies provide 50% more experience gained when slain.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_7: Rare enemies provide 200% + additional 4% per level, which means that level 100 rare enemies provide 600% more experience when slain.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_9: Boss enemies do not have an experience gain multiplier, but have a much higher base experience reward when slain than other enemies.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_10: If a lower level player is in a much higher level area, they gain experience from slaying enemies as if the area was up to 10 levels higher than their character. For example, a level 20 character in a level 40 area would gain experience as if the area was level 30.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_11: When playing together with other players and there are big level differences, the previous 10 level difference can go down to a minimum of 2, based on the level difference between the characters. For example, if a level 10 character and a level 70 character were playing together in a level 40 area, the level 10 character would gain experience as if the area was level 12, and the level 70 will gain experience from level 40 area as normal.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_12: Players that are 5 or more levels below the starting level of a chapter will gain less experience from completing quests relative to their character level. For example, completing quests in Chapter 9 will grant much less experience to a character that is level 5, than to a character that is level 50.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_13: Additional bonuses which increase the experience gained in <link="arena">Arena</link> and Monolith Echoes won’t apply to characters under level 50, but they will still gain the unmodified amount of experience from slain enemies.
GameGuide.Experience_Paragraph_14: The amount of <link="terminology">Favor</link> gained while aligned with an <link="item factions">Item Faction</link> is based on the experience you gain.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_0: Stash Priority lets you define rules for how certain items should be moved into your stash when quick storing (shift + right click or X / Square on controller). If any tab has a matching priority when quick storing an item, it will be placed in that tab, even if not currently viewed. Manually placing items directly in a slot in a tab bypasses Stash Priority.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_2:
<#E5E5E5>Configuring Stash Priority</color>
You can set priority conditions on any tab when configuring it (right click the tab or use the configure tab button while viewing it) by checking the Stash Priority checkbox. To remove priority conditions, uncheck this and save the tab.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_3:
Stash Priority supports the following conditions, similar to <link="loot filter">Loot Filters</link>:
Item Type
- Subtype (if only 1 item type is selected)
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_4:
<link="Rarity">Rarity</link>
- <link="legendary items">Legendary Potential</link> Min/Max (if only Unique is selected)
- <link="weaver''s will">Weaver''s Will</link> Min/Max (if only Unique is selected)
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_5:
Class Requirement
- For example, you can set a tab to only acceptitems if they can be equipped by a Priamlist or a Mage.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_6:
Level Requirement
- For example, a tab could be set to only accept items if they have a minimum level requrement of 80 to equip, or a maximum level of 70 to equip.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_7:
<link="item factions">Item Faction</link> Requirement
- For example, some items drop with a Circle of Fortune requirement, and all items traded between players in Merchant''s Guild will require to be part of the Merchant''s Guild to equip.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_8: All priority conditions on a tab must match for an item to be automatically placed there.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_9: For example, a tab with priority conditions of Rarity: Exalted and Item Type: Helmet will match exalted helmets, but not exalted boots or unique helmets.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_10:
<#E5E5E5>How Priority Chooses Tabs To Send Items To </color>
You can set priority conditions on any tab when configuring it (right click the tab or use the configure tab button while viewing it) by checking the Stash Priority checkbox. To remove priority conditions, uncheck this and save the tab.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_11: When multiple stash tabs have a priority that matches an item, it will be placed in the first tab that matches and has space for the item. This respects your custom ordering and will pick the leftmost tab in the leftmost category that matches.
GameGuide.StashPriority_Paragraph_12: If there is no stash tab with matching priority, or all tabs with matching priority do not have space to fit the item, it is instead placed in the currently viewed tab if possible.
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_0: The stash supports searching for items based on the contents of their tooltip as well as macros, regex, and expressions to compose more specific searches.
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_1: When searching in the Quick View sidebar, your tabs will be filtered to only show those that contain at least one matching item.
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_2: Usage Examples - T6+ or 1T6+ matches any exalted item (at least 1 affix is tier 6 or higher) - 2T7 matches double T7 exalted items (at least 2 affixes are tier 7) - 3T6+&T7 matches triple exalted items where at least 1 affix is T7 (e.g. T7/T7/T7 or T7/T6/T6 would both match) - WW&PT20+ would match Weaver''s Will items that have 20 or more Weaver''s Will and legendary affix tiers - LP3+|WW20+ to find high potential uniques - prefixes1&T7 to find T7 exalts with an open prefix - T7&boots to find boots with at least 1 T7 affix - relic&/1[4-6] dexterity/&suffixes1- to find relics with T7 dexterity and at least 1 open suffix.
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_3: Regex - Wrap your search in / to search using case-insensitive regex - e.g. /1[4-9] attunement/ to find items with 14-19 attunement
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_4: Macros Macros are case-insensitive short hands that match supported properties of items with an optional quantifier e.g. - LP0 (is unique with no legendary potential) - T6+ (has tier 6 or higher affix) - prefixes2 (has 2 prefixes) Most macros match a number on the item and are of the form: Macro[number][+/-] If a number is provided, the item must exactly match that number. If + or - is provided, the item must be greater/less than or equal to that number. For example: - WW matches any Weaver’s Will item and the macro matches the amount of Weaver’s Will on the item - WW0 matches any Weaver’s Will item with no Weaver’s Will left - WW15+ matches any Weaver’s Will item with at least 15 Weaver’s Will
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_4_A:
Macros can be negated with ! to invert what they match
- !Corrupted matches items that are not corrupted
- !Trade matches items that are not tradable
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_5: Expressions Macros and regex can be combined into expressions - Combining with | means either the left or right macro must match - Combining with & means both the left and right macro must match
GameGuide.StashSearching_Paragraph_6: Supported Macros Item Potential - LP (is non-WW unique) - WW (is WW unique or legendary) - WT (is enchantable idol) - FP (is forgeable equipment) - PT (potential tier) matches items that could be used for unique rerolling in the Gauntlet of Strife.

GameGuide.Shrines_Paragraph_0: Shrines are objects that a player can interact with to activate them. There is a wide variety of different effects and buffs that occur when they are activated. For example, they can spawn creatures to aid you in combat, drop items, buff the player or cast skills while the shrine is active.
GameGuide.LootLizard_Paragraph_0: Loot Lizards are peaceful creatures burdened by the weight of items they carry. You can help unburden them by attacking them. They will flee when attacked.
GameGuide.LootLizard_Paragraph_1: There are several different types of Loot Lizards that carry different items, and they can be distinguished from each other by their color.
GameGuide.LootLizard_Paragraph_3: When reduced to zero health, Loot Lizards will escape. If they have not been damaged for 20 seconds, they will also escape. This timer will reset whenever any damage is dealt to them.
GameGuide.Champions_Paragraph_1: Champions are a subset of Rare enemies, with proper names and more powerful abilities. They often have their own modifiers, which do not spawn on other enemies. They can be recognized by their names, minimap icon, and an orange highlight.
GameGuide.Champions_Paragraph_2: Once defeated, Champions always drop an item with a sealed Champion Affix based on the Champion''s modifiers. Champion Affixes only occur on items, they cannot be obtained as shards via <link="runes and glyphs">Rune of Shattering</link> or <link="runes and glyphs">Rune of Removal</link>.
GameGuide.RiftBeasts_Paragraph_1: Rift Beasts are ancient and powerful creatures that possess the ability to tear rifts between eras. This allows them to hunt down their prey with swift ambushes wherever and whenever they please.
GameGuide.RiftBeasts_Paragraph_3: Sometimes Rift Beasts leave larger rifts behind that lead to their dens in the Ancient Era, where they lay their eggs and prepare for future hunts. After defeating a Rift Beast in its den, you can choose which of its offspring survives, effectively deciding how future Rift Beasts you encounter will have evolved.
GameGuide.RiftBeasts_Paragraph_5: Different evolutions cause the Rift Beasts to gain different abilities and grow different body parts. Some of these body parts can be harvested and exchanged with Skarven Bloodhorn for powerful items such as <link="primordial items">Primordial Unique items</link> and <link="runes and glyphs">Runes of Evolutions</link>.
